scope: Cross-correspondent knowledge only: incoming wedding-related letters to Darwin versus Darwin outgoing letters dated November 1838 through April 1839. Existing direct links 456→483, 487→489, and 504→506 are excluded from proposed links.

incoming_reviews.summary: Caroline Wedgwood congratulates Darwin on his engagement and says the family at Shrewsbury is pleased.
incoming_reviews.attribution: Caroline Wedgwood's incoming voice; the editorial note identifies 11 November as the engagement date.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: Strong source for Darwin's explicit later report to Emma that he had received a letter from Caroline.

incoming_reviews.date_assessment: 14 November [1838], single day with editorially supplied year.
incoming_reviews.summary: Charlotte Langton warmly congratulates Darwin and expresses confidence in his and Emma's happiness.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: No distinctive Charlotte detail is repeated in the examined Darwin outgoing letters.

incoming_reviews.summary: William Owen Sr replies to Darwin's news, promises to tell his dispersed family, and invites Darwin and his future wife to Shrewsbury.
incoming_reviews.attribution: William Owen Sr's incoming voice; family references remain his report.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: No examined Darwin outgoing letter identifies Owen's letter or repeats a distinctive Owen detail.

incoming_reviews.date_assessment: 22 November [1838], single day with editorially supplied year.
incoming_reviews.summary: Harriet Henslow congratulates Darwin, jokes about domestic life, and hopes he will still visit the Henslows at Christmas.
incoming_reviews.attribution: Harriet Henslow's incoming voice; Mr Henslow's proposed visit is reported within her letter.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: Its Christmas invitation overlaps the already accepted 456→483 chain, but 483 cannot be separately attributed to Harriet rather than J. S. Henslow.

incoming_reviews.date_assessment: 4 December [1838], single day with editorially supplied year.
incoming_reviews.summary: Charlotte Langton thanks Darwin, reports meeting Emma, and praises Emma's reception into the family and the plan to help choose a London house.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: The examined house-related outgoing letter 448 predates 450; later Darwin house reports do not name Langton or repeat her distinctive reception wording.

incoming_reviews.summary: J. S. Henslow wishes Darwin marital happiness and asks whether he will visit at Christmas on Mrs Henslow's behalf.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: Existing accepted direct link 456→483; excluded from new cross-correspondent proposals.

incoming_reviews.date_assessment: 13 January [1839], single day with editorially supplied year.
incoming_reviews.summary: J. M. Herbert sends an earwig-shaped silver asparagus server as a wedding gift and offers congratulations.
incoming_reviews.attribution: J. M. Herbert's incoming voice; the editorial note identifies the Forficula as an asparagus utensil.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: Existing accepted direct link 487→489; excluded from new cross-correspondent proposals.

incoming_reviews.summary: William Whewell presents Hermann und Dorothea as a marriage gift and sends good wishes.
incoming_reviews.attribution: William Whewell's incoming voice; the book is identified editorially as his private translation.
incoming_reviews.candidate_use: Existing accepted direct link 504→506; excluded from new cross-correspondent proposals.

outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin personally announces his engagement to Charles and Mrs Lyell.
outgoing_witness_reviews.attribution: Darwin voice; he is the source of the engagement news, so this is not knowledge derived from incoming 431.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: No incoming wedding letter is needed to explain this announcement.

outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin writes Emma about the family's welcome, London versus suburban housing, and Caroline's letter after the engagement.
outgoing_witness_reviews.attribution: Darwin voice; the named Caroline is a reported correspondent, not an inserted editorial voice.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: Supports new 431→437 knowledge link in paragraph 3.

outgoing_witness_reviews.date_assessment: 21 November 1838 postmark date; editorial note says Darwin misdated it.
outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin recounts travel, FitzRoy's advice about married life and houses, and a Lyell letter forwarded from Shrewsbury.
outgoing_witness_reviews.attribution: Darwin voice; FitzRoy, Lyell, and Mrs Lyell are reported sources.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: No distinctive content from incoming 439 is named; the Lyell correspondence is a separate chain.

outgoing_witness_reviews.date_assessment: 23 November [1838], single day with editorially supplied year.
outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin answers C. T. Whitley's kind letter by announcing his marriage to Emma, the January wedding plan, and intended London life.
outgoing_witness_reviews.attribution: Darwin voice; the kind letter addressed in paragraph 1 is Whitley's unlocated letter, not William Owen's 439.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: No incoming 439 knowledge edge is supported.

outgoing_witness_reviews.date_assessment: 30 November–1 December 1838, two dated writing sections; paragraph 7 is Saturday morning.
outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin writes Emma about letters from Catherine, house hunting, servants, Lyell's advice, and Emma's coming to London.
outgoing_witness_reviews.attribution: Darwin voice; Catherine and Lyell's sister are reported correspondents, not Darwin's incoming wedding sources.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: The house/visit material predates incoming 450 on 4 December, so 450 cannot be its source.

outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin reports securing 12 Upper Gower Street, furniture and servants, and his eagerness to enter the house with Emma.
outgoing_witness_reviews.attribution: Darwin voice; no incoming wedding correspondent is named.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: No distinctive detail ties it to Langton 450 or another incoming wedding letter.

outgoing_witness_reviews.date_assessment: 4 January [1839], single day with editorially supplied year.
outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin updates Whewell on Jukes and asks him to thank Henslow and Mrs Henslow for a letter and Cambridge invitation while mentioning house hunting before marriage.
outgoing_witness_reviews.attribution: Darwin voice; Henslow and Mrs Henslow are reported correspondents.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: The accepted 456→483 link is not duplicated; Harriet 442 is a possible overlapping invitation witness but not a separately identifiable source.

outgoing_witness_reviews.date_assessment: 16 April [1839], single day with editorially supplied year.
outgoing_witness_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Whewell for the marriage gift and comments on Hermann und Dorothea and the History of the inductive sciences.
outgoing_witness_reviews.relevance: Existing accepted 504→506 direct link is not duplicated.

proposed_links.reason: Darwin's 14 November letter to Emma explicitly says he had a letter from Caroline the previous day and characterizes its expressions as concerning both Darwin and Emma. Caroline Wedgwood's 11 November incoming letter is the surviving Caroline wedding letter in this bounded set and contains the matching engagement congratulations. This is a knowledge witness, not a claim that 431 is a prompt for Darwin's own announcement or that its composition date is receipt date.
proposed_links.scope: DCP-LETT-437 paragraph 3: Caroline's congratulatory expressions only.

evidence.quote: you will be as happy as happy can be & I do most heartily rejoice
I had a letter from Caroline yesterday, full of kindest & tenderest expressions towards us both.

rejected_or_qualified_candidates.reason: Harriet's Christmas-visit invitation overlaps Darwin's thanks to Henslow and Mrs Henslow in 483, but the already accepted 456→483 link supplies a direct J. S. Henslow letter with the same invitation. 483 does not identify Harriet's earlier letter as its source, so no second edge is added.

evidence.quote: I do hope this event will not put a stop to the visit Mr Henslow has held out hopes of, of your coming to us at Christmas
thank him from me for his letter & Mrs Henslow for her invitation to Cambridge

rejected_or_qualified_candidates.reason: 450 is dated 4 December, whereas 448's final Saturday-morning section is 1 December. The later Langton advice about Emma helping choose a house cannot be the source of the earlier outgoing passage; the house overlap is generic and the outgoing names no Langton report.

evidence.quote: I think this is a capital plan of her going up & helping you to choose a house
I was delighted to receive your letter: nothing in the world could be more fortunate than your being able to come to town

rejected_or_qualified_candidates.reason: Although both involve marriage news and 443 says 'your kind letter', 443 is addressed to C. T. Whitley and its referenced letter is Whitley's unlocated correspondence. Owen 439 cannot be substituted on shared congratulations or date proximity.

evidence.quote: the glad Tidings you have communicated
I have been very long in answering your kind letter

unlocated_references.description: The physical Caroline letter Darwin says he received is not otherwise preserved in the outgoing record; 431 is the surviving identified candidate.
The Henslow letter and invitation are represented by the accepted 456→483 chain; Harriet's separate 442 invitation cannot be independently assigned as the source.
Whitley's 'kind letter' prompting 443 is not among the eight wedding-related incoming records.

limitations: Incoming composition dates are not treated as receipt dates; 437's resolved writing date establishes only that 431's content was known by 14 November if 431 is the identified Caroline letter.
The accepted direct links 456→483, 487→489, and 504→506 are intentionally omitted from proposed_links, though their source records were read to prevent duplicate cross-correspondent claims.
Congratulatory wording, family overlap, and house-hunting topics are not treated as knowledge evidence without explicit naming, distinctive content, or chronology.
No claim is made that incoming correspondents supplied Darwin's voice; all incoming passages remain witness evidence only.
